Remember, it's okay to feel shy, and most people can relate to feeling a bit nervous

In group conversations, I listen attentively and try to contribute when I feel comfortable, often by asking questions or sharing opinions softly. I avoid dominating the conversation and give others plenty of space to speak. I also make an effort to maintain eye contact, but only briefly, to show respect without feeling overwhelmed.

I might bring along a book or something to occupy my hands, like a notebook or a sketchpad, to have a low-key activity to focus on if needed. And, of course, I always appreciate it when there's a quiet corner or a chance to take a break away from the main gathering.

Remember, it's okay to pace myself and not force myself to be constantly social. Sometimes, just being present and observing can be a way to participate without feeling too exposed.

I might avoid eye contact or prolonged direct conversations, fearing that I might say something inappropriate or embarrass myself. I prefer one-on-one interactions or smaller groups, where I can contribute without feeling too exposed.

I might also bring along a friend or someone I trust to provide support and make me feel less alone. And, of course, I'll make sure to pace myself and not overextend myself, knowing that it's okay to take breaks when needed. Overall, I navigate these situations with caution and a sense of self-compassion, embracing my shyness while still trying to enjoy the experience.

I usually take some time to prepare myself mentally and gather my thoughts before approaching a situation. I might practice what to say or think of a few ice-breaker questions beforehand to help ease the conversation.

When entering a new environment, I try to observe and listen carefully to others, which helps me feel more comfortable. I might start by introducing myself softly and briefly, focusing on building rapport with a simple comment about the event or shared interests. I'm not very good at small talk, so I might ask open-ended questions to show genuine interest without overwhelming myself.

I also appreciate it when there's a clear structure or purpose for the gathering, as that gives me a sense of direction. I might seek out friendly faces or individuals who share similar interests to make the interaction more manageable.

Throughout the encounter, I'll maintain eye contact but not too intense, and I'll be mindful of my body language, ensuring it's relaxed and approachable. If the situation allows, I prefer to have one-on-one conversations rather than large group settings, as it feels less intimidating.

Remember, it's okay to feel shy, and most people can relate to feeling a bit nervous

6. **Take breaks**: It's okay to step away for a moment
